According to Saleh, Elliott went to his car and retrieved the weapon following an altercation with offensive tackle JC Latham during practice on 15 October. The 28-year-old did not play in Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts and was cut Tuesday over what the club described as an “incident.”
Saleh described Elliott as a father and a good husband who has no criminal history, and said the decision to grab a gun suggested Elliott may be crying out for help and that something larger could be going on.
Latham called the altercation unfortunate and said it happened in the heat of the moment. He said there was no bad blood between the two players and no argument leading up to it, adding that mental health is extremely important and that he hoped Elliott gets support.
Elliott, who has also played for San Francisco and Cleveland, appeared in five games this season. Saleh said he would still recommend Elliott to another team, saying he would vouch for his character while acknowledging that rules against guns on team property must be followed.
